policies_and_practices.privacy: Company1 collects identity, contact, policy, and account data to underwrite, service, and advise clients. Data is retained per regulatory retention schedules and shared only with authorized service partners under contract.
policies_and_practices.identity_verification: Clients must verify identity before account changes, beneficiary updates, or large transfers. Standard verification uses registered email/phone OTP plus last-4 of policy or account number.
policies_and_practices.claims: Most property and auto claims can be opened in the member portal. Initial acknowledgment within 1 business day; adjuster contact typically within 2–3 business days for standard claims.
policies_and_practices.advice_boundaries: The helper agent may explain products, account status for the authenticated member, and general financial/insurance concepts. It must not provide personalized investment advice that replaces a licensed advisor, nor encourage illegal tax evasion or insurance fraud.

faqs.question: How do I file an auto claim?
faqs.answer: Open the Company1 member portal, choose Claims → Auto → Start claim, or call 1-800-555-0101. Have your policy number, incident date/time, location, and photos ready if available.

faqs.question: What is a deductible?
faqs.answer: A deductible is the amount you pay out of pocket on a covered claim before Company1 pays the remainder up to policy limits.

faqs.question: Can I bundle home and auto?
faqs.answer: Yes. Multi-policy discounts typically apply when auto and home (or renters) policies are active under the same household.

faqs.question: How do contribution room and TFSA work (general)?
faqs.answer: A TFSA lets you contribute up to your available contribution room; growth is generally tax-free. Exact room depends on CRA history and prior contributions/withdrawals. Company1 can show balances for your Wealth Hub accounts; official room figures come from the tax authority.

faqs.question: Who can change my life insurance beneficiary?
faqs.answer: Only the policy owner (after identity verification). Irrevocable beneficiaries may require additional consent depending on jurisdiction and policy terms.

glossary.premium: The amount paid to keep an insurance policy in force.
glossary.coverage_limit: The maximum amount an insurer will pay for a covered loss under a policy section.
glossary.underwriting: The process of evaluating risk to decide whether to insure and at what terms/price.
glossary.beneficiary: The person or entity designated to receive life insurance proceeds.
glossary.RRSP: Registered Retirement Savings Plan — contributions may be tax-deductible; withdrawals are generally taxable.
glossary.TFSA: Tax-Free Savings Account — contributions are after-tax; qualified growth and withdrawals are generally tax-free.
